note: Proposed logical architecture; validate during discovery.
description: Serverless multi-brand conversational platform in ap-south-1 serving App, Web and WhatsApp customers, integrating TUL's existing enterprise systems and customer-service platform with Bedrock-powered AI.

steps.title: Customers start conversations
steps.description: Customers open the chat widget through CloudFront or message on WhatsApp, and the WhatsApp provider forwards signed webhooks to API Gateway.

steps.title: Messages queued in order
steps.description: API Gateway passes each message to Lambda handlers, which queue it in SQS so a worker can process every conversation in order with retries.

steps.title: Bot reasons with knowledge
steps.description: The conversation worker calls Bedrock for chat handling under Guardrails and retrieves FAQ and policy passages from Knowledge Bases to ground its answer.

steps.title: Verify and act on orders
steps.description: When account data is needed, Lambda sends outbound calls through the NAT gateways to verify the customer with the OTP service and reach SAP Hybris via the enterprise API gateway.

steps.title: Replies and proactive notifications
steps.description: Lambda sends bot replies back through the WhatsApp provider and turns incoming business events into messages sent through the notification providers.

steps.title: Handover to live agents
steps.description: When escalation rules match, Step Functions runs the handover workflow, Lambda creates the case in the customer-service platform, and agents continue the chat there.

steps.title: Agents and admins sign in
steps.description: Agents and admins sign in through Cognito, which federates to the TUL corporate IdP for single sign-on.

steps.title: Knowledge articles synced
steps.description: On an EventBridge schedule, Lambda exports articles from the customer-service platform and stages them in S3, and Knowledge Bases then ingests them into its index.

steps.title: Conversation analytics and dashboards
steps.description: DynamoDB stream changes trigger Lambda to report conversation events through Firehose to the data lake, Redshift then loads them for analytics, and QuickSight dashboards query the results.
